questions.solution:
Given,

${S}_{1}: {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - x - y - \dfrac{1}{2} = 0$

So, the centre is ${C}_{1}: \left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ and the radius is ${r}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2}} = 1$

${S}_{2}: {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 4y + \dfrac{7}{4} = 0$

So, the centre is ${C}_{2}: \left(0, 2\right)$ and the radius is

${r}_{2} = \sqrt{4 - \dfrac{7}{4}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

${S}_{3}: {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 4x - 2y + 5 - {r}^{2} = 0$

So, the centre is ${C}_{3}: \left(2, 1\right)$ and the radius is

${r}_{3} = \sqrt{4 + 1 - 5 + {r}^{2}} = \left|r\right|$

From the diagram, we can say that if $A ∪ B ⊆ C,$ then the circle $A \text{ and } B$ should lie in the circle $C$

Here, ${C}_{1}{C}_{3} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}$

So, $\left\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}} \le \left|r - 1\right| ⇒ \begin{array}{ll}r \le 1 - \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}} \\ r \ge 1 + \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}\end{array}\right\}$

Also, ${C}_{2}{C}_{3} = \sqrt{5} \le \left|r - \dfrac{3}{2}\right|$

$⇒ \left\begin{array}{ll}r \ge \sqrt{5} + \dfrac{3}{2} \\ r \le \dfrac{3}{2} - \sqrt{5}\end{array}\right\}$

So, the minimum value of $r = \dfrac{3 + 2\sqrt{5}}{2}$

questions.q: The points of intersection of the line $ax + by = 0$, $( a \ne b )$ and the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2x = 0$ are $A ( \alpha, 0 )$ and $B ( 1, \beta )$. The image of the circle with $AB$ as a diameter in the line $x + y + 2 = 0$ is :
questions.solution:
Given,

The points of intersection of the line $ax + by = 0, ( a \ne b )$ and the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2x = 0$ are $A\left(\alpha, 0\right)$ and $B ( 1, \beta )$ then,

For point $A\left(\alpha, 0\right)$

$a ( \alpha ) + b ( 0 ) = 0 ⇒ \alpha = 0$

And, ${\alpha}^{2} - 2\alpha = 0 ⇒ \alpha = 0, 2$

For point $B ( 1, \beta )$

$a + b\beta = 0$

Or, $\beta = \dfrac{- b}{a}$

And, $1 + {\beta}^{2} - 2 = 0$

$⇒ \beta = \pm 1$

$∵ a \ne b$ therefore,

Only possibility $\alpha = 0, \beta = 1$

Points are $A\left(0, 0\right)$ and $B\left(1, 1\right)$

So the centre of the circle with diameter AB is $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ and radius $r = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Now the image of $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ about the line $x + y + 2 = 0$ is,

$\dfrac{x - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = \dfrac{y - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = \dfrac{- 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} + 2\right)}{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = \dfrac{y - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = - 3$

$⇒$Centre of image circle is $\left(- \dfrac{5}{2}, - \dfrac{5}{2}\right)$

Equation of image circle

${\left(x + \dfrac{5}{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left(y + \dfrac{5}{2}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 5x + 5y + 12 = 0$

questions.solution:
Given,

A point $P$ moves so that the sum of squares of its distances from the points $\left(1, 2\right)$ and $\left(- 2, 1\right)$ is $14$.

So, ${\left(x - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(x + 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 1\right)}^{2} = 14$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + x - 3y - 2 = 0$

Put $x = 0$

$⇒ {y}^{2} - 3y - 2 = 0$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{2}$

Put $y = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + x - 2 = 0$

$\left(x + 2\right)\left(x - 1\right) = 0$

$∴ A\left(- 2, 0\right), B\left(1, 0\right), C\left(0, \dfrac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{2}\right), D\left(0, \dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2}\right)$

Area formed by $ACBD$ will be $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}- 2 & 0 \\ 0 & \dfrac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{2} \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2} \\ - 2 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left|- 3 - \sqrt{17} - \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{2} + 3 - \sqrt{17}\right|$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times \sqrt{17} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{17}}{2}$ sq units.

questions.q: A ray of light through $\left(2, 1\right)$ is reflected at a point $P$ on the $y -$ axis and then passes through the point $\left(5, 3\right) .$ If this reflected ray is the directrix of an ellipse with eccentricity $\dfrac{1}{3}$ and the distance of the nearer focus from this directrix is $\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{53}},$ then the equation of the other directrix can be:
questions.solution:
The reflected point of $\left(2, 1\right)$ is $\left(- 2, 1\right) .$

Equation of reflected ray

$y - 1 = \dfrac{3 - 1}{5 + 2}\left(x + 2\right)$

$⇒ y - 1 = \dfrac{2}{7}\left(x + 2\right)$

$⇒ 7y - 7 = 2x + 4$

$⇒ 2x - 7y + 11 = 0$

Let the equation of other directrix is

$2x - 7y + \lambda = 0$

Distance of directrix from focus

$\dfrac{a}{e} - ae = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{53}}$, where $e$ is the eccentricity

$⇒ 3a - \dfrac{a}{3} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{53}}$ or $a = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{53}}$

Distance from other focus $\dfrac{a}{e} + ae$

$= 3a + \dfrac{a}{3} = \dfrac{10a}{3} = \dfrac{10}{3} \times \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{53}} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{53}}$

Distance between two directrix $= \dfrac{2a}{e}$

$= 2 \times 3 \times \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{53}} = \dfrac{18}{\sqrt{53}}$

So, $\left|\dfrac{\lambda - 11}{\sqrt{53}}\right| = \dfrac{18}{\sqrt{53}}$

$⇒ \lambda - 11 = 18$ or $- 18$

$⇒ 2x - 7y - 7 = 0$ or $2x - 7y + 29 = 0$

Now equation $\left(1\right) \div$equation $\left(2\right)$ we get,

$\dfrac{{b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} = \dfrac{4}{7} \cdot \dfrac{{b}^{3}}{{a}^{3}}$

$∴ 7a = 4b ⋯ \left(3\right)$

From $\left(2\right)$

$\dfrac{\dfrac{16{b}^{2}}{49} + {b}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = \dfrac{11}{4} \cdot \dfrac{16{b}^{2}}{49b}$

$77a + 44b$

questions.q: Let $P$ be a variable point on the parabola $y = 4{x}^{2} + 1 .$ Then, the locus of the mid-point of the point $P$ and the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $P$ to the line $y = x$ is:
questions.solution:
We have,

$y = 4{x}^{2} + 1$

$L: y = x$

Let the foot of perpendicular from $P$ to line $y = x$ is $Q$.

Let $P ≡ \left(x, y\right)$, $Q ≡ \left(c, c\right)$ and $R ≡ \left(h, k\right)$ where, $R$ is the mid-point of $PQ$.

Clearly,

$PQ ⊥ L$

$⇒ \dfrac{k - c}{h - c} = - 1$

$⇒ c = \left(\dfrac{h + k}{2}\right)$

And,

$R ≡ \left(\dfrac{x + c}{2}, \dfrac{y + c}{2}\right)$

$⇒ R ≡ \left(\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{h}{4} + \dfrac{k}{4}, \dfrac{y}{2} + \dfrac{h}{4} + \dfrac{k}{4}\right)$

Hence,

$h = \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{h}{4} + \dfrac{k}{4} ⇒ x = \dfrac{3h}{2} - \dfrac{k}{2}$

$k = \dfrac{y}{2} + \dfrac{h}{4} + \dfrac{k}{4} ⇒ y = \dfrac{3k}{2} - \dfrac{h}{2}$

Now,

$y = 4{x}^{2} + 1$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{3k - h}{2}\right) = 4{\left(\dfrac{3h - k}{2}\right)}^{2} + 1$

$⇒ \left(3k - h\right) = 2{\left(3h - k\right)}^{2} + 2$

Required locus is

$2{\left(3x - y\right)}^{2} + \left(x - 3y\right) + 2 = 0$
